messages:
sre-bot: PAGER: P1 - Veridian (dedicated pool VERI-P1) - elevated model errors and tail latency. Paging oncall now.
ryan_oncall: on it. joining call in 2.
ryan_oncall: ping @maria_ml for model context — customer running hybrid rerank+generate, seeing 5xx and long tails.
maria_ml: saw increased logits collapse around 15:03 UTC, retries and duplicate tokens. error rate ~3% of requests, spike started ~14:55.
sam_platform: infra telemetry shows sudden KV cache evictions on VERI-P1 GPUs starting 14:50, eviction_rate=1200/s, memory_pressure=0.92.
ryan_oncall: is this isolated to one cluster or across the tenant?
sam_platform: single dedicated pool (VERI-P1) for Veridian. other pools normal.
ken_netops: network looks fine, no packet loss. this is compute/memory pressure.
liz_custsuccess: flagging customer support. Veridian on enterprise SLA; need impact summary for CS.
maria_ml: hypothesis: model variant uses large KV caches; variant v3.0-highmem recently rolled two days ago. maybe memory regression.
ryan_oncall: OK plan: 1) pin traffic to previous safe variant (v2.9-safe) via routing override; 2) scale up pool if needed; 3) notify customer and keep canary for 10m.
liz_custsuccess: I'll draft a short note: "We're applying a temporary model routing fix to reduce errors, working on a permanent fix."
sre-bot: INCIDENT: created incident/INC-2026-4112, Pager duty alert linked.
ryan_oncall: doing model override now in console. command: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/internal/route_override -d '{"customer":"veridian","override":"model:v2.9-safe","duration":"15m"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN"```
maria_ml: Nice. Also suggest turning on prefix KV caching for rerank paths to reduce cache churn. small config: `kv_cache_policy: prefix_only`
sam_platform: applying instance bump as well: adding 2 nodes to VERI-P1, scaling should be up ~30s.
ryan_oncall: overrides applied. routing shows 100% to v2.9-safe. monitoring graphs... error rate dropping.
ken_netops: eviction_rate down to 120/s and memory_pressure -> 0.65.
maria_ml: model-level errors down to baseline ~0.2%. latency tail improving.
liz_custsuccess: sending update to Veridian contacts: "We observed a model variant memory regression; we rolled traffic back to a verified safe variant and scaled pool. We will follow up with root cause and timeline."
ryan_oncall: temp mitigation successful. next: collect logs for the v3.0-highmem rollout, replicate in staging. @maria_ml can you lead validation?
maria_ml: yes, will repro with customer prompt set and stress KV cache. scheduling a canary in staging with same config.
sre-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled in 45m to next engineer @ryan_oncall remains primary until mitigation confirmed.
ryan_oncall: adding runbook note: `veridian-override-1769993333`: pinned to v2.9-safe, scaled +2 nodes, set kv_cache_policy prefix_only, monitor for 1h.
liz_custsuccess: Veridian acknowledged, appreciates the quick rollback. asking for ETA on permanent fix. I'll coordinate with AM.
ken_netops: leaving a sticky alert to auto-scale if memory_pressure > 0.85 for 10m.
maria_ml: started deeper trace. initial signs point to a memory leak in attention cache allocation path in v3.0. will open a PR with a patch candidate.
ryan_oncall: good. please include regression tests. once patch ready, we'll schedule a controlled rollout with canary and fallback pin.
liz_custsuccess: updating ticket: impact window ~14:55-15:07 UTC, ~12 minutes, affecting ~2.3% of requests with degraded outputs. mitigation applied at 15:03.
ryan_oncall: moving to monitoring. will handoff to day SRE in 40m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam_platform: cluster stabilized, leaving autoscale policy active.
maria_ml: PR opened: #4821, adding guard for kv allocation and unit test. tagging @sam_platform for review.
sre-bot: INCIDENT: update - mitigation verified, switched to 'monitoring' stage.
ryan_oncall: final note: do not re-roll v3.0-highmem until PR validated and a canary passes. I'll close incident when 1h stable.
liz_custsuccess: preparing final customer postmortem draft for AM review.
ryan_oncall: closing slack thread, will update incident doc with timelines and links.
